new_statements.quote: Dalam BS nada, panjang, dan tekanan tidak fonemik. [...] Dalam BS tekanan sudah dapat diperkirakan sebelumnya. Pada umumnya tekanan jatuh pada suku kedua untuk kata-kata yang terdiri dari dua suku atau lebih. Karena tekanan itu sudah dapat diperkirakan sebelumnya, maka disimpulkan bahwa tekanan tidak fonemik dalam BS. Kata deriq 'dari' baik diucapkan dengan tekanan pada suku pertama atau pada suku kedua tidak berubah artinya. Tekanan mungkin saja dapat mengubah arti (fonemik) dalam ujaran yang lebih panjang, misalnya dalam frase atau kalimat, tapi dalam penelitian ini tidak dibicarakan mengingat keterbatasan waktu yang disediakan.
new_statements.translation: In BS [bahasa Sekak] pitch, length and stress are not phonemic. [...] In BS stress is predictable. In general stress falls on the second syllable in words consisting of two or more syllables. Because stress is predictable, it is concluded that stress is not phonemic in BS. The word deriq 'from', whether pronounced with stress on the first syllable or on the second, does not change its meaning. Stress may possibly change meaning (be phonemic) in utterances longer than the word, e.g. in phrases or sentences, but that is not discussed in this study given the limited time available.
new_statements.citation: Napsin, Syahrul, Zainal Abidin Naning, Selamet Abdullah & Zulkarnain Mustafa. 1981. Struktur bahasa Sekak. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa. xv+192 pp.
new_statements.locator: Section 2.4 'Fonem Suprasegmental', book pp. 55-56 (PDF pp. 69-70); restated in 5.1 Kesimpulan, book p. 153 (PDF p. 167): 'Hasil analisis fonem suprasegmental menunjukkan bahwa dari keempat jenis fonem tersebut yang signifikan dalam BS adalah jeda.'
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (40,076,274 bytes, 206 pp., Adobe ClearScan text layer, the PDF's metadata OK). extracted text gives section '2.4 Fonem Suprasegmental' with book page footers 55 and 56, and I rendered PDF pp. 69-70 to PNG and read the page images. The whole quoted passage is on those two pages exactly as the reader gives it: p. 55 'Fonem suprasegmental meliputi nada (pitch), panjang (length), tekanan (stress), dan jeda (juncture). Dalam BS nada, panjang, dan tekanan tidak fonemik.'.. 'Dalam BS tekanan sudah dapat diperkirakan sebelumnya. Pada umumnya tekanan jatuh pada suku kedua untuk kata-kata yang terdiri dari dua suku atau lebih. Karena tekanan itu sudah dapat diperkirakan sebelum-' / p. 56 'nya…
new_statements.relation_note: lonc1237 is not in the catalog and has no existing statements; this is the first sourced word-stress statement for the language and would be a new entry (fixed: second syllable, non-contrastive, per Napsin et al. 1981 pp. 55-56). Not a contradiction of anything on record.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is predictable and non-contrastive; in general it falls on the second syllable of words of two or more syllables (counted from the left, as the text says 'suku kedua', not 'suku kedua dari akhir'). Since most Sekak lexemes are disyllabic this coincides with final-syllable stress for the bulk of the vocabulary; for longer words the text literally puts it on the second syllable. Juncture (jeda) is the only suprasegmental the authors treat as phonemic.
new_statements.exceptions: Hedged with 'pada umumnya' (in general). The word deriq 'from' can be stressed on either syllable with no change of meaning. Pitch and length are also stated to be non-phonemic (nada tinggi sekali used for anger; /ke:neng/ ~ /ke:ne:ng/ 'now' same meaning). Possible meaning-bearing stress at phrase/sentence level is explicitly left unstudied.
new_statements.identity_note: Napsin et al. 1981 describe 'bahasa Sekak' (BS), the language of the Orang Laut / suku Sekak of Bangka: data from the resettlement villages at Kecamatan Pangkalan Baru (people from Pulau Semujur) and Jebu (Kecamatan Jebus), with smaller groups on the Lepar and Pongok islands and the Belinyu coast (book pp. 8-9). The authors state there is no dialectal variation (1.9 Variasi Dialektal, p. 9-10; repeated in the Kesimpulan p. 152). ISO 639-3 CR 2015-008 (already held by the project) equates Sekak/Sekah with [lce] Loncong.

Re-download from a network that can reach Indonesian.go.id hosts, or from a copy of the repository mirror.
